downloads.why_relevant: This is the automotive answer to our exact problem, and it is the single best template for Q2/Q3. They face the same trilemma - full-wave is unaffordable for a moving articulated dielectric body, scattering-centre models are cheap but their reflectivities are 'loosely approximated by RCS values of primitives' and therefore wrong in magnitude, and SBR is accurate but too slow for per-pulse simulation. Their answer is a HYBRID: run SBR once on the poly-mesh to learn point-scatterer reflectivities by linear regression, then run the cheap model at PRF. That is a methodology we could borrow directly.

verbatim.quote: Two commonly used simulation methods are: the computationally simple scattering center model of dynamic humans; and the shooting and bouncing ray technique based on geometric optics. The latter technique is more accurate but due to its computational complexity, it is usually used only for modeling scattered returns of still human poses. In this work, we combine the two methods in a linear regression framework

A slightly less computationally expensive alternative is based on shooting and bouncing rays and geometric optics and has been used for predicting the RCS of still humans at X-band and Ku-band frequencies [30-32]. However, the technique still remains computationally expensive and cannot be used to generate radar data at the pulse repetition frequency
We adapted the fairly standard shooting and bouncing ray technique proposed in [35] on the poly-mesh human data for RCS estimation for different polarizations and aspect angles

answers_the_starred_question.question: Does anyone publish a USABLE PTD correction to PO?
answers_the_starred_question.answer: Partly. The literature publishes a FORMULATION and an IMPLEMENTATION RULE, not a closed-form 'band-slope correction factor'. This paper gives the ray-level acceptance criterion (d_hit < lambda/10 from the edge) that makes PTD attachable to an SBR loop. The Bilkent thesis (D-OZTURK-BILKENT-PTD) gives the underlying equivalent-edge-current machinery. NOBODY I found publishes a per-band multiplicative correction you could apply to a PO answer after the fact.
answers_the_starred_question.confidence: medium - based on 6 targeted searches, not an exhaustive survey

caveats: No quantified dB improvement from adding PTD is stated in any sentence I extracted; the with/without comparison is presented as figures. Figures may be image-only - the dB delta is UNVERIFIED.

downloads.why_relevant: ⭐ Gives a HARD, quotable validity bound on the method family we use, and INDEPENDENTLY corroborates the lambda/10 FACET-size criterion that the Montaner dispute (X-C10) turns on - and it is unambiguous that lambda/10 there is the FACET edge length, which is exactly the E5 correction our own record already made.

verbatim.quote: Since, high-frequency techniques are used in calculations, what restricts the application of this computer program is the fact that the size of the scatterer must be large in terms of the wavelength at the given frequency (e.g. ka > 10 for a sphere).
The computer program assumes the value of lambda^2/200 for the area of a facet. In other words, each facet is assumed to be equilateral triangles of edge length no more than lambda/10.

By high-frequency phenomena, it is meant that fields are being considered in a system where the properties of the medium and scatterer size parameters vary little over an interval on the order of a wavelength. In other words, what restricts the application of a high-frequency method is the fact that the size of a scatterer must be large in terms of the wavelength at the given frequency.

There are three RCS regimes that characterize the relationship between the wavelength and the body size: Low-Frequency scattering, resonant scattering and high frequency scattering. In this thesis, the attention is focused on calculating the RCS of a perfectly conducting body with arbitrary shape in the high frequency scattering region.

Method of equivalent edge currents (EEC) is a powerful technique in the analysis of scattering. Any finite current distribution yields a finite result for the far-zone diffracted field when that distribution is summed in a radiation integral. Thus, the invalidity of the GTD diffraction at the caustics can be avoided by the use of a proper current distribution on the edge.

load_bearing_for: report06/07 honest scoping of PO+PTD validity
caveats: GREY. A 2002 MSc thesis is fine as corroboration and as a source for standard formulae; it is NOT a citation of record for a headline claim. Pair it with a peer-reviewed source before it appears in a report.

⭐ NOTE THE SELF-INCRIMINATING BIT: 'ka > 10 for a sphere'. At 3.5 GHz (lambda = 8.57 cm), ka > 10 needs a >= 13.6 cm radius, i.e. a ~27 cm sphere. A DJI Mini-class body does NOT clear that bar in our band. This source, read honestly, bounds our own method more tightly than our reports currently do.

verbatim.quote: A perfect electrically conducting (PEC) hexagonal prism with a circle-cylinder shaped duct. A fan-blade assembly is inserted into the duct.
In these problems, the model sizes are in the range 0.013 <= L/lambda_0 <= 438, where lambda_0 is the free-space wavelength.

scattering from the smallest camera box at frequencies f in {10, 20, 40, 80, 160, 320, 640, 1280, 2560, 5120, 7000, 10240} MHz are included in the problem set. This distortion is because of publicly available measurement data [1]

The VV-polarized RCS pattern at 2.56 GHz for the smallest problem in the problem set was found to exhibit unusually high sensitivity to computational errors and simulation parameters in the 15o <= phi_i <= 30o range [3]. Methods and parameters that typically yield sufficiently accurate results may yield results that agree poorly with the reference simulation and measurement data for this part of the pattern.

Compute VV- and HH-polarized RCS patterns / CFIE, alpha = 0.5 / Mesh ZA, lambda_0/13.1, 72 693 RWGs / Most of look-angles agree with measurement; notable exception in sigma_theta_theta ... f = 2.56 GHz L = 40 cm

CFIE formulation can still lead to inaccuracy for certain types of geometries / Holes, thin surfaces, small gaps, etc. / Has been demonstrated for pedagogical examples, but what about realistic geometries?

on_disk_discoveries.why_this_matters: Everything we have been missing in one package: (a) 2.56 GHz - within a factor 1.4 of our 3.5 GHz carrier; (b) L = 40 cm at 2.56 GHz is L/lambda ~ 3.4, i.e. the SAME few-wavelength regime where our PO f^2 slope is suspect; (c) it contains rotating-fan-like blades in a duct, the geometric motif of a drone rotor; (d) TWO independent measurement runs plus an independent reference simulation, so the measurement uncertainty is itself bounded; (e) the problem set spans L/lambda from 0.013 to 438, so we could measure OUR OWN solver's error as a function of electrical size and find where our PO stops working - empirically, in our own band, against measured truth. Nothing else found in this hunt does that.
on_disk_discoveries.recommended_action: Run our SBR+PO against IIISD s1 at f9=2.56 GHz, both polarisations, and plot our error versus the two measurement runs and the reference simulation. Then sweep the L/lambda ladder to locate our own validity floor. This converts 'PO is a best-fit approximation' from an assertion into a measured number.
on_disk_discoveries.bears_on_H8: INDIRECT but important. It does not refute H8. It does remove our excuse: it means a validated in-band scattering computation IS checkable with data we already have, so 'nobody has validated one' cannot be extended into 'nobody could'.
caveats: PEC only. No dielectrics, no carbon fibre, no battery.
The 4th data column's unit is UNVERIFIED - read IIISD_Data_file_descriptor.pdf first.

The two IEEE AP Magazine 2025 benchmark papers are NOT on disk and are paywalled; the methodology statements above come from the problem-description PDF and the ACES 2024 slides, not from those papers.

ptd_and_frequency_slope.the_question: Our band slope is too steep because PO keeps only the f^2 specular term with no PTD. How does the CEM literature handle it, and does anyone publish a usable correction?

what_I_can_state_with_evidence.claim: The high-frequency method family is explicitly scoped to electrically large scatterers, with a concrete numeric bound.
what_I_can_state_with_evidence.evidence: D-OZTURK-BILKENT-PTD p.69 verbatim: 'the size of the scatterer must be large in terms of the wavelength at the given frequency (e.g. ka > 10 for a sphere)'.
what_I_can_state_with_evidence.implication_flagged_as_our_derivation: ka > 10 at 3.5 GHz (lambda = 8.57 cm) requires a >= 13.64 cm, i.e. a ~27 cm equivalent sphere. This is OUR arithmetic, not the thesis's.

what_I_can_state_with_evidence.claim: PTD is added to PO by an equivalent-edge-current (EEC) integral; the total field is the PO surface integral plus the edge-diffracted field.
what_I_can_state_with_evidence.evidence: D-OZTURK-BILKENT-PTD p.45 verbatim on EEC. Corroborated at web-search level by the IEEE TAP 'Iterative Physical Optics With Physical Theory of Diffraction' abstract (ieeexplore 9727080) - NOT DOWNLOADED, so that corroboration is UNVERIFIED.
what_I_can_state_with_evidence.status: VERIFIED for the EEC sentence; UNVERIFIED for the IPO-PTD corroboration

what_I_can_state_with_evidence.claim: There is a published, implementable acceptance rule for attaching PTD to an SBR loop of our architecture.
what_I_can_state_with_evidence.evidence: D-KIRIK-SIGMA-PTD-SBR p.3 verbatim: 'the diffraction contribution of this particular ray is included in PTD result if d_hit is less than the maximum permitted distance of d_max = lambda/10'.

what_I_can_state_with_evidence.claim: An asymptotic (ray) solver's error concentrates AWAY from specular directions - stated by an independent measurement group about their own CST run.
what_I_can_state_with_evidence.evidence: D-SEMKIN-ACCESS-2020 p.5 verbatim: 'Differences are visible away from the specular reflections due to the asymptotic solver used in the simulations.'

what_I_can_state_with_evidence.claim: Even full-wave CFIE has geometry-specific errors on ducted, thin-surface, small-gap geometries at 2.56 GHz.
what_I_can_state_with_evidence.evidence: OD-AUSTIN-IIISD-FANBOX, ACES2024presentation.pdf p.4 and p.8 verbatim.

what_I_could_NOT_establish: NO source found publishes a usable post-hoc CORRECTION FACTOR - a multiplier or a dB-per-GHz adjustment - that converts a PO answer into a PTD-corrected one. The literature publishes formulations and implementation rules, and expects you to recompute.
NO quantified 'PTD adds X dB of accuracy' number was extracted from any PDF. The Sigma paper's with/without-PTD comparison is presented in figures which may be image-only. UNVERIFIED.

The frequently repeated claim that edge-diffraction RCS scales differently from the specular f^2 term appeared ONLY in web-search summaries, and the two summaries I got were mutually inconsistent (one said 'frequency independent', another said 'decreases as lambda^-1/2'). NO PDF sentence was obtained. ⚠ DO NOT PUT A SCALING EXPONENT FOR EDGE DIFFRACTION IN ANY REPORT ON THE STRENGTH OF THIS HUNT. It is exactly the E1/E3 shape - a plausible equation with no document behind it.
The MITRE report ADA286329 and the NATO STO 'Drone RCS Statistical Behaviour' paper, both of which looked likely to carry regime-boundary tables, could not be downloaded (blocked).

empirical_slope_evidence_gathered.note: The only NEW empirical constraint this hunt produced on the frequency slope. All inputs are verbatim-quoted dBsm values from D-EZUMA-TAES-PREPRINT pp.24-25; the per-drone slopes and the summary statistics below are OUR DERIVATION computed in the build script, NOT numbers printed in the paper.
empirical_slope_evidence_gathered.band: 15 -> 25 GHz, VV polarisation, compact-range anechoic chamber, azimuth-averaged 'average RCS'
empirical_slope_evidence_gathered.reading: Two of the six drones (DJI Matrice 600 at +4.35 dB and Trimble zx5 at +4.75 dB) sit essentially ON the pure-PO f^2 prediction of 4.44 dB, while the DJI Mavic Pro at +0.86 dB is nearly flat. So at 15-25 GHz - where these airframes are tens of wavelengths - f^2 is NOT uniformly wrong; it is right for the large carbon-fibre platforms and wrong for the small plastic one. That pattern is consistent with, but does NOT prove, the hypothesis that the f^2 term fails as the target approaches a few wavelengths. It also means our slope problem cannot be blamed on PO alone: it is band- AND platform-dependent.
empirical_slope_evidence_gathered.apples_to_apples_warning: ⚠ H5 asks whether Yuan's and Das's slopes are the same statistic. The same question now applies to Ezuma. Ezuma's Tables II-V give 'mu' and 'Std' in dBsm and the text calls it 'average RCS', but NO sentence I extracted defines whether the average is taken in linear or dB domain. Until that is read, these three slope families MUST NOT be plotted on one axis. Marking UNVERIFIED.
empirical_slope_evidence_gathered.second_warning: These values are from the arXiv PREPRINT. Re-check against IEEE TAES 58(1):27-46 before any of them reaches a figure.

ptd_and_frequency_slope.recommendation: Stop arguing the slope from theory. Run the IIISD 2.56 GHz benchmark (OD-AUSTIN-IIISD-FANBOX) and measure our own PO error against measured truth in our own electrical-size regime. That is a one-afternoon experiment with data already on disk, and it replaces an unciteable scaling argument with a number.

H8_attack_report.hypothesis: H8: zero PUBLISHED papers compute a validated scattering signature from a drone mesh in a Sionna-class engine.
H8_attack_report.verdict_after_this_hunt: NOT REFUTED, but the wording needs tightening in two places.

attacks_attempted.attack: Automotive - someone must have validated a mesh-derived signature against measurement.
attacks_attempted.result: They have: D-DEEP-IETRSN-PEDESTRIAN (PUBLISHED, IET RSN 2020) runs SBR on a human poly-mesh and compares range profiles and spectrograms against measured automotive radar data. It does NOT refute H8 (pedestrians, not drones; no Sionna-class engine) but it DOES refute any looser wording such as 'nobody validates ray-traced mesh signatures'. ⭐ ACTION: check report01's H8 sentence for that looser wording.

attacks_attempted.attack: Computational EM - someone must have done full-wave on a drone.
attacks_attempted.result: They have: D-LEE-JEES-MOM-DRONE (PUBLISHED, JEES 2021) does MoM/RWG on DJI Mavic 2 propellers at 9.65 GHz. Does not refute H8: no Sionna-class engine, propellers only, and validation is solver-vs-solver rather than against measurement.

attacks_attempted.attack: Drone RCS measurement papers - someone must have simulated the mesh they measured.
attacks_attempted.result: D-SEMKIN-ACCESS-2020 (PUBLISHED, IEEE Access 2020) runs the CST Integral-Equation solver on a drone model at 28 GHz for per-part attribution. Does not refute H8: not a Sionna-class engine, and the simulation is used qualitatively rather than validated quantitatively against their own measurement.

attacks_attempted.attack: Is there an open-source Sionna-class engine that already does this?
attacks_attempted.result: open-rcs (github.com/comp-ime-eb-br/open-rcs) - open-source PO+GO RCS platform for 3D targets, monostatic and bistatic, apparently a Python descendant of POFACETS. NOT DOWNLOADED, NOT INSPECTED. It is a PO/GO code, not a Sionna-class differentiable engine, so on current information it does not refute H8 - but it is the closest tool-level competitor found and it should be checked, both as an H8 attack and as an independent cross-check of our own PO.

H8_attack_report.residual_risk: MEDIUM. Every H8 attack I could mount from open web search failed for the same structural reason - the communities that validate are not using Sionna-class engines, and the community using Sionna-class engines is not validating. That is a real gap, not an artefact. But this hunt was six search threads deep, not exhaustive, and I did not search non-English literature or theses.
wording_recommendations: Keep 'drone' and 'Sionna-class engine' in the sentence. Both qualifiers are load-bearing; drop either and the claim is false.
Prefer 'validated against measurement' over 'validated' - the JEES paper is validated against another solver and would otherwise be a counter-example.
State the search scope. 'We found none in X searches across these communities' survives scrutiny; 'zero papers exist' does not.

THREE NEW VERSION-DRIFT TRAPS FOUND, all in material this hunt downloaded: (1) arXiv:2112.09774 'Classification' published as IEEE Sensors Journal 'Recognition' - the TITLE changed; (2) the Notaros/Troksa SBR manuscript on disk says 'electromagnetic modeling' where the published TAP title says 'propagation modeling'; (3) arXiv:2411.03206's own title differs from the title search engines return for it. The Ziganshin lesson generalises: in this literature, title drift between preprint and publication is common, not exceptional.

recommendations: ⭐1. Run our SBR+PO against Austin RCS Benchmark Problem Set IIISD at 2.56 GHz (measured runs m1 and m2 plus the reference simulation, both polarisations, meshes included) and publish the error. The data is already on disk. This is the cheapest available conversion of an assertion into a measurement, and it is IN OUR BAND and IN OUR ELECTRICAL-SIZE REGIME. Read IIISD_Data_file_descriptor.pdf first to fix the units, and get the Kelley AMTA 2023 paper for the measurement uncertainty before quoting any error number.
2. Sweep the IIISD L/lambda ladder (the set spans 0.013 to 438) to locate our own solver's validity floor empirically, rather than asserting one.
3. Add /data/public/sionna_jeong/sionna2_archive/reference_cad/reference_study to the ledger's archive_inventory. 45 PDFs and the whole benchmark-suite tree are currently invisible to it.

4. Re-check every Ezuma number against IEEE TAES 58(1):27-46 before it reaches a figure, and settle the 'average RCS' statistic definition before any slope from Ezuma, Das or Yuan shares an axis with another.

5. Borrow the Deep et al. hybrid explicitly in report07 or report08: run the expensive mesh solver ONCE offline to calibrate a cheap parametric model, then run the cheap model at PRF. Cite it as the automotive precedent. It is PUBLISHED (IET RSN 2020, DOI in the arXiv metadata), which is stronger support than most of our current citations.
6. Tighten H8's wording per h8.wording_recommendations - 'drone' and 'Sionna-class engine' and 'validated against measurement' are all load-bearing qualifiers.

7. Do NOT write any edge-diffraction frequency-scaling exponent into a report on the strength of this hunt. No PDF sentence was obtained and the two web summaries contradicted each other. This is the E1/E3 shape.

8. Second-pass downloads worth another try: the MDPI/Sensors automotive sensor-model survey (closest existing analogue to our Q2 catalogue), the two IEEE AP Magazine 2025 Austin benchmark papers, Kelley AMTA 2023, Held TMTT 2022, and the open-access Rahman Scientific Reports 2018 micro-Doppler paper.
9. Inspect github.com/comp-ime-eb-br/open-rcs - it is both an H8 attack surface and a free independent cross-check of our PO facet integral.
